column1: # Forbric kernel -- Minecraft-line rename table for 1.21.1
# The runtime source set (src/runtime/java) is written in the 26.2 namespace. A second Minecraft line gets
# the table below applied at build time, because every entry here is a MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE name: it exists on
# one line and does not exist on the other. Re-measure, do not trust this sentence:
# So no single spelling compiles on both lines, and a blanket rename in the sources is not available. Each
# entry below was checked in BOTH directions against the staged merged bases
# and, where a member is involved, against the method signature with `javap`.
# Format: <26.2 name> TAB <1.21.1 name>   ('#' starts a comment; blank lines ignored)
# Rules are applied longest-first and whole-token only ((?<![A-Za-z0-9_$]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9_$])), so
# `Identifier` never reaches inside `KernelIdentifier` and a fully-qualified rule always wins over its own
# simple name. The build FAILS if a rule matches nothing, so a table entry that has gone stale is an error
# Mojang renamed ResourceLocation -> Identifier in 26.x. Same class, same members: parse, tryParse,
# tryBuild, fromNamespaceAndPath, withDefaultNamespace, getNamespace, getPath all exist on both sides
# A member rename, not a class rename. 26.2 ResourceKey has `Identifier identifier()` and no `location()`;
# 1.21.1 ResourceKey has `ResourceLocation location()` and no `identifier()` (javap both). 17 call sites,
# all on a ResourceKey. TagKey#location() already has this name on BOTH lines, so it is left alone -- the
# rule rewrites `identifier()`, which TagKey never had.
# Renamed to MobSpawnType. Verified through the method that consumes it: 1.21.1
# MobSpawnType.SPAWNER / NATURAL / MOB_SUMMONED / TRIGGERED / TRIAL_SPAWNER all exist.
# 26.2 split the entity constants (EntityTypes) from the registry type (EntityType); 1.21.1 has both on
# EntityType, whose ZOMBIE / DROWNED / ZOMBIE_VILLAGER / SKELETON / SPIDER are public static finals. A
# whole-token rule, so `EntityType` written already -- which the sources never do -- would be untouched.
# net.minecraft.world.entity.vehicle.Boat (1.21.1). 1.21.1's `Boat` is what the type is for -- it carries
# the paddle constants and is the common base of the boat family.
# 26.2 moved three entity classes into their own subpackages; 1.21.1 keeps them flat. Simple names unchanged.
# 26.2 split the particle registry/reload-listener (ParticleResources) away from the ticking engine
# (ParticleEngine); 1.21.1 has the two roles on ParticleEngine, which is the class that implements
# PreparableReloadListener and owns the `providers` map the kernel reads on both lines. Role-based mapping,
# which is why it is written down: it is the one entry here that is not a literal rename.
# EventBus 7 gives every event class its own static typed bus (`X.BUS`). EventBus 6.2.33 has no such field
# anywhere; the same event is posted on the one game bus, whose declaration was read out of the staged 1.21.1
# Each rule below is therefore a claim that THIS event belongs on the game bus on 1.21.1 -- not "BUS lives
# somewhere else". The claim was measured per event, two ways, before the rule was written:
#   (a) the event does not implement `net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent` on 1.21.1 (javap), and
#   (b) where the Forge hook is reachable, its bytecode posts it with
# Both spellings appear where the sources use both, because the substitution is textual: a rule written for
# the short form would otherwise fire inside the fully qualified one. Longest-first ordering is what keeps
# that honest, and a rule that matches nothing fails the build.
# SITES THAT LOOK EXACTLY LIKE THE RULES ABOVE AND MUST NOT GET ONE. Each would compile and be wrong:
#       Both fire on the MOD event bus. In 6.2.33 that bus has NO name: it is reached through
#       FMLJavaModLoadingContext.get().getModEventBus(), an expression, and this file maps names. Pointing
#       them at EVENT_BUS would compile and silently deliver the event to nobody -- the exact failure mode
#   LivingEvent.LivingVisibilityEvent.BUS    Same. net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.IEventBus in 6.2.33 has no
#       hasListeners() at all (javap: register, addListener x4, addGenericListener x4, unregister, post x2,
#       fire x2, shutdown, start). Rewriting the receiver would trade "cannot find symbol BUS" for "cannot
#       find symbol hasListeners" -- one error for another, which is not a fix and would move the error out of
#       this axis's count for no reason.
#       Those three inner classes do not exist on 1.21.1. This is the 26.x capability-provider split already
#       recorded in docs/1.21.1-port.md stage 3 (1.21.1 CapabilityProvider has 2 inner classes, 26.2 has 7).
# --- measured absent, with no same-simple-name counterpart anywhere in 1.21.1 -----------------------
# Every class in the staged 1.21.1 jars was indexed (12,505) and searched by simple name for each of these
# (build/x11/find-counterparts.py). At most four candidates came back per name and each was a different
# concept. These are a whole API generation, not a spelling.
#                                                   that is a different platform, not a rename.
#   net.neoforged.fml.jarcontents.JarContents       26.x only; no jarcontents package on 1.21.1.
#                                                   through its item-extension/RenderTooltip path; there is no
#       The KEYED listener registry is 26.x. See the ordered-listener note below.
#       26.x sorted-listener events: the kernel calls `SortedReloadListenerEvent.addListener(key, listener,
#       order)`. 1.21.1 HAS the older pair -- net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent -- so the event exists and the ORDERED API does
#       not. That is a design difference (the kernel depends on listener order), not a rename.
#   net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result            absent: 1.21.1's common.util has 90 classes and neither
#                                                   Result nor TriState. The kernel's use is the
#                                                   net.minecraft.util.TriState is itself absent on 1.21.1, so
#                                                   the cluster is blocked on axis 1, not on this name.
#                                                   AnvilUpdateEvent is a different event, not a new name.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.block.BreakBlockEvent     THE ONE REAL RENAME IN THIS LIST, and still
#       not a rule. 26.x un-nested the class; 1.21.1's is
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.BlockEvent$BreakEvent, and javap shows the SAME constructor
#       (Level, BlockPos, BlockState, Player), the SAME getPlayer()/setCanceled(boolean) and the same
#       superclass, so the three call sites would compile. It is left out because a name rule cannot express
#       the target cleanly: it is a NESTED class, and the file using it already imports a DIFFERENT
#       MinecraftForge event a few lines later. The only spelling that works is the `$` form,
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.BlockEvent$BreakEvent, which does compile but puts a `$`-nested
#       type into source that never otherwise uses one -- for three errors. Written down instead of ruled,
#       so the next agent does not have to re-derive that the rename exists.
#   net.minecraftforge.client.gui.overlay.ForgeLayer no overlay-layer API before 26.x; the same axis-1
#                                                   Hud/Gui split as the entry in the tail above.
#       Both belong to 26.x's picture-in-picture pipeline, and 1.21.1 has no
#       net.minecraft.client.gui.render.pip package at all (axis 1 tail above).
#       NeoForge's OWN transfer API, added after 1.21.1: there is no net.neoforged.neoforge.transfer package in
#       the 1.21.1 jars at all. This is the largest error group in both axes and it is a whole API generation.
#       It is NOT the fabric transfer axis -- see AXIS 3 below, where that claim is measured.
# AXIS 3 -- fabric-api transfer 0.116.17 vs 8.0.11, and Team Reborn Energy
# THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The 26.2 and 1.21.1 transfer modules were extracted
# separately (build/x11/transfer-26.2/, build/x11/transfer-1.21.1/) and their class lists diffed:
#     present on BOTH: ItemVariant, FluidVariant, Storage, StorageView, Transaction, TransactionContext,
#                      SlottedStorage<ItemVariant> and both have of(Container, Direction) + getSlots() +
# `ResourceHandler`/`EnergyHandler`/`TransactionContext` are NOT fabric names at all -- they come from
# net.neoforged.neoforge.transfer.*, which is why they appear in the axis-2 list above. What the error
# splitter calls "axis 3" is NeoForge-transfer errors plus Team Reborn Energy errors; the fabric transfer API
# itself contributes three ContainerStorage errors and a staging problem.
# WHY ContainerStorage -> InventoryStorage IS DELIBERATELY NOT A RULE. Applying it is measurably a lateral
# takes INTERMEDIARY names. The kernel calls `ContainerStorage.of(container, Direction.UP)` with Mojmap types,
# so after the substitution the three "cannot find symbol ContainerStorage" become three "incompatible types:
# Container cannot be converted to class_1263" -- same total, different bucket -- and the real gap stays
# hidden behind a rename that looks like a fix. The gap is that the 1.21.1 fabric-api modules are
# intermediary-remapped: the same cause produces the 20 `class_1937 / class_2248 / class_2338 / class_2350 /
# class_1792 / class_1935 / class_3611 / class_9326` errors. The fix is to remap those three modules to
# Mojmap (tools/namespace/ already builds the table), not to rename a type.
# TEAM REBORN ENERGY IS A STAGING DEFECT, NOT AN API DIFFERENCE. All 12 classes of
# .dev/api/energy-5.0.0.jar are class-file 69 (Java 25), and a JDK-21 `--release 21` javac cannot read the jar
#         class file has wrong version 69.0, should be 65.0
# Every `team.reborn.energy.*` reference then fails as `cannot find symbol`, which is 24 of the errors the
# splitter calls axis 3. Handled OUTSIDE this table, because it is not a name: the jar's class-file version is
# retargeted to 65 with every other byte identical (build/x11/retarget-jar.py: 12 classes, bytes 0-5 and
# 8-end compared equal), and the ABI is then proven unchanged by the repository's own check --
# Measured effect of that alone: 608 -> 587 total, axis3 166 -> 142. The 1.21.1 line still needs a real
# Java-21 build of that jar; the retarget is a local staging repair, not a substitute for one.
# DELIBERATELY ABSENT -- measured as absent from 1.21.1 and NOT a rename. These need the code restructured,
# which changes 26.2 too, so they are not table entries. Adding one of them here makes the build compile and
#   net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.FuelValues     fuel values are a furnce-block-entity concern
#   net.minecraft.server.packs.metadata.pack.PackFormat   pack format is an int before 1.21.9
#   net.minecraft.client.gui.Hud                          the HUD is Gui/GuiGraphics before 26.x
#   net.minecraft.client.gui.render.pip.*                 picture-in-picture renderers do not exist pre-26.x
#   net.minecraft.util.random.WeightedList                API differs, not a name: 1.21.1 has no Builder
# MEMBER-level counterparts checked with javap and NOT expressed as rules, because each one changes the shape
# of the expression rather than a name. Kept here so the next agent does not have to re-derive them:
#       1.21.1 has no PackFormat at all, and the consumer differs too: 26.2 builds
#       PackMetadataSection(Component, InclusiveRange<PackFormat>) while 1.21.1 takes an int pack format.
#       KernelClientPackSource needs a real branch, not a substitution.
#   Gui.overlay() / Gui.hud                (26.2) -> no counterpart: 1.21.1 has no Gui/Hud split
#   Minecraft.gui.setScreen/screen()/disconnectWithSavingScreen would be ten clean renames, but they are
#   EXPRESSION fragments (`gui.` disappears), so they are deliberately not rules: this file maps names, and
#   mixing in expression rewrites would make it mean two different things. Their containing files are blocked
